lines: It helped keep the wolves from making a story of me. That's enough praise.
It did the job when fear was loud. That's praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
The straps held when I had to run. I checked them afterward.
This piece took a hit that would have reached me.
The edge stayed sharp through the whole fight.
I used it in the rain, and my grip never slipped.
There is a dent here from the first blow. Better the gear than my ribs.
It was light enough to move in and strong enough when I could not.
I had to repair the buckle, but the rest came through clean.
The padding stopped the worst of an arrow strike.
I trusted it once the fighting began and forgot about it until the end.
It caught on a fence during the retreat. That needs fixing.
The weight tired me sooner than I expected.
I would shorten this strap before taking it out again.
It protected my shoulder when a raider got too close.
The blade held up, though it needs a proper sharpening now.
I used every part of it except the bit I thought would matter most.
It came back stained and scratched, but it came back with me.
For real trouble, I would carry it again.
Unused so far. I prefer watching over nervous sheep to testing nervous steel.
It has stayed wrapped since you gave it to me.
No trouble has come close enough for me to draw it.
I tried the fit by the pen, but that is all.
The straps sit well. I cannot speak for how they hold in a fight.
It has been waiting beside my bed every night.
I keep it clean in case the bell rings.
The flock has seen more of it than any enemy has.
I practiced with it once, well away from the lambs.
There is no wear to report beyond dust from the shelf.
I carried it on patrol without needing it.
The balance feels right, though fear may change that.
I adjusted the buckle before storing it.
It is ready. I am glad I do not know more yet.
No arrows, claws, or blades have tested it.
I wore it through one false alarm and took it off at dawn.
The edge is still exactly as you left it.
I have checked it often enough to trust the fastening.
If trouble comes, I will not have to learn where I put it.
Ask me again after it has done more than wait.
